items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: So Kid Rene, he had the hottest jazz band around town. ... But none of them could surpass Kid Rene. That's fabulous.

ctx.x: We had Earl. So Earl he left and he went away. And so we got a fellow called Thomas. Sorry I can't think of Thomas. He died three years ago. We got Thomas. And the band was playing real good, really good. So Kid Rene, he had the hottest jazz band around town.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: But Kid Rene, I used to play that number, with Kid Rene.

ctx.x: What was he like to work for?

Buddy is a wonderful trumpet player. But he played different from Kid Rene, in that he liked to run a lot of different, we used to call that changes, because of his horn. But if you would hear Louis Armstrong's old record, just like listening to Buddy Petit. But I don't mean Louis' late record, where he played all high in his pretty well. In the beginning, when he first started playing, he started to record in the ring of 20s, that you could get some of the records, you'd listen to Buddy Petit. Yeah.

You said that, remember that number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes? You said that was one of Buddy's numbers? Is that where you first heard that number? By Buddy playing it? Did I? That number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes. I understand. Is that where you first heard that number, by Buddy Petit playing it, or did you?

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: And we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone

ctx.x: Was he doing a range here in the band? Was he doing a range here?

Yeah, he'd do some range, he was doing a range. And we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone, but Louis Russell did all of that. After that band broke up, we went on the road. We had trombone played, they did all the business. Pete, I can't think of his name unless I look up the name.
I think I have it outside in the car. Yeah. I didn't want to get it if you wanted to.
